name: Interstitial Lung Disease Specific to Infancy

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Infantile Interstitial Lung Disease Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Persistent tachypnea, hypoxemia, and respiratory distress in infancy
High-resolution CT showing diffuse interstitial infiltrates and ground-glass opacities
Lung biopsy demonstrating interstitial thickening with alveolar septal fibrosis and inflammatory infiltrates
Exclusion of infectious etiologies by microbiological testing
Identification of mutations in surfactant protein genes (e.g., SFTPC, ABCA3)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of clinical presentation plus characteristic radiologic findings and histopathology consistent with interstitial lung disease in infancy
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Lung biopsy is often required for definitive diagnosis; genetic testing can support diagnosis and guide prognosis.

searchTerms: low oxygen levels not improving with oxygen therapy
oxygen therapy failing to raise blood oxygen

common.symptomName: Failure to thrive due to increased work of breathing
searchTerms: poor growth due to breathing difficulty
failure to gain weight from breathing strain
growth problems from increased breathing effort
bluish skin during feeding or activity
turning blue with exertion or eating

occasional.symptomName: Mild hepatomegaly secondary to right heart strain
searchTerms: slightly enlarged liver from heart strain
mild liver swelling due to right heart issues

rare.symptomName: Developmental delay secondary to chronic hypoxia
searchTerms: growth and learning delays due to chronic hypoxia
slow developmental milestones from oxygen deficiency

laboratory: Arterial blood gas showing hypoxemia and respiratory alkalosis
Elevated inflammatory markers may be present
Normal or mildly elevated white blood cell count
imaging: High-resolution CT scan showing diffuse ground-glass opacities, interstitial thickening, and cystic changes
Chest X-ray with reticulonodular infiltrates and hyperinflation
genetic: Mutations in surfactant protein genes (SFTPC, SFTPB, ABCA3)
NKX2-1 gene mutations in some cases
other: Lung biopsy demonstrating alveolar septal thickening, fibrosis, and inflammatory infiltrates
Pulmonary function tests showing restrictive pattern (if feasible)

distinguishingFeatures: Localized cystic lung lesions on imaging
Presence of infectious agent on cultures
History of prematurity and prolonged oxygen therapy
Radiologic evidence of airway remodeling rather than diffuse interstitial disease

redFlags: Progressive respiratory failure despite supportive care
Severe hypoxemia unresponsive to oxygen supplementation
Failure to thrive with worsening respiratory symptoms
references: Nathan N, et al. Interstitial lung disease in infancy: clinical features and outcomes. Pediatr Pulmonol. 2022;57(3):567-577.
Orphanet: Interstitial lung disease specific to infancy. ORPHA:264694.
Young LR, et al. Genetic causes of pediatric interstitial lung disease. Pediatr Res. 2021;89(4):765-773.
